title: China-to-Azerbaijan Lithium Battery & Power Bank Compliance Gap Matrix
provenance: AI-compiled, multi-model cross-checked, not human-verified. Informational only; confirm with the official regulator and a qualified professional. Not legal/certification/customs/market-access advice.

rows.requirement: AZSTAND Import Conformity Regime for Lithium Batteries and Power Banks
rows.target_requirement: AZSTAND is the mandatory conformity framework for regulated import products in Azerbaijan. Where lithium batteries and power banks are within scope, market entry requires compliance documentation against the applicable national standard route, which may reference AZS adoptions of IEC and GOST text, and customs release is tied to import-side verification before distribution in country. Imported products typically require in-country importer coordination at the port of entry in Baku for market entry checks and any post-clearance surveillance steps.
target_standards: AZSTAND import conformity framework and mandatory market entry procedures
AZS technical references and national adoptions of IEC and GOST standards for conformity assessment
rows.china_equivalent: China baseline compliance is typically based on GB 31241 safety requirements and, where applicable, CCC certification and national customs filing. This creates domestic gatekeeping, but it is not the same process as AZSTAND import conformity in Azerbaijan, and there is no one-step import equivalence.
china_standards: GB 31241 — safety requirements for portable sealed secondary lithium cells and batteries for use in portable electronic equipment
CNCA CCC certification (where applicable) and GACC customs declaration requirements
rows.gap: The target-market process is importer-led and regulation-specific, while China documents stop at domestic safety or certification. Chinese outputs may provide test evidence, but they do not complete AZSTAND entry or in-country compliance filing in Azerbaijan.

mandatory_status.target: Mandatory for regulated products in scope, where AZSTAND import conformity and in-country coordination is required before market entry.
mandatory_status.cn: Mandatory for products falling under CN domestic catalogues (GB 31241 baseline, CCC where applicable), but not equivalent in scope to Azerbaijan import procedures.

rows.verdict: [INFORMATIONAL] Chinese GB 31241 and CCC documentation is useful but does not complete Azerbaijan AZSTAND import conformity flow. Exporters should plan for Azerbaijan-specific conformity pathways, local importer alignment, and in-country file completion prior to Baku entry.

source.publisher: AZSTAND, Azerbaijan State Standardization, Metrology and Patents Service

rows.requirement: Portable Lithium Cell and Power Bank Safety — AZS/IEC 62133
rows.target_requirement: Azerbaijan references AZS-aligned IEC 62133 requirements for lithium cell and power bank safety. Although local publication structure differs, import checks in practice rely on equivalent safety criteria for abuse, mechanical integrity, and electrical protection. In-market acceptance is tied to product-level evidence for the exact model variant and may require national authority review for regulated products.
target_standards: AZS-referenced IEC 62133 safety requirements for portable lithium batteries
National adoption notices that align with IEC 62133 for import control
rows.china_equivalent: China baseline is GB 31241. GB 31241 provides a comparable safety baseline for portable sealed secondary lithium cells and batteries, but its test evidence is domestic in framing and must be mapped into Azerbaijan import expectations for each model.
china_standards: GB 31241 — safety requirements for portable sealed secondary lithium cells and batteries for use in portable electronic equipment
CNCA safety and product certification practice for charged lithium products
rows.gap: Model-level mapping is the key gap. GB 31241 reports may be used as technical support, but Azerbaijan expects local conformity context and import-side validation tied to AZS route obligations and local importer coordination.

mandatory_status.target: Mandatory where AZS-constrained import categories require compliance proof for the exact model and safety parameters.
mandatory_status.cn: Mandatory for domestic categories tied to CN safety and certification rules; not in itself sufficient for Azerbaijani import acceptance.

rows.verdict: [INFORMATIONAL] GB 31241 reports are useful baseline evidence but are not a full substitute for Azerbaijan in-market safety review pathing. Exporters should align documentation model-by-model and confirm that each battery variant is accepted under the AZS-based route.

rows.requirement: EMC, Radio, and Product Marking Requirements
rows.target_requirement: Azerbaijan applies destination-side EMC and radio expectations for products with communication functions, alongside national conformity handling for regulated electrical products. Conformity is not achieved by safety test certificates alone, and CE is not generally a standalone substitute in this lane. Importers should treat EMC and radio functions as separate compliance dimensions and ensure correct local approvals when applicable.
target_standards: AZS-based electrical safety and EMC handling for regulated imports
National radio regulator route for communication-capable products
rows.china_equivalent: China relies on GB/T EMC standards and radio authorization channels such as SRRC/MIIT for transmit-capable devices. These outputs support export readiness but do not complete Azerbaijani in-country EMC and radio filing when the Azerbaijani route requires specific importer or authority interaction.
china_standards: GB/T 9254 / GB/T 17743 EMC framework for Chinese products
SRRC and MIIT radio authorization practice in China
rows.gap: The target market separates communication-related compliance from general safety compliance, while Chinese exports commonly bundle documentation under domestic EMC and SRRC routes. Exporters should confirm whether national radio approval is required in Azerbaijan and obtain the local channel through the in-country importer.

mandatory_status.target: Conditionally mandatory for products with radio transmission functions and for categories requiring local EMC evidence.
mandatory_status.cn: Mandatory where Chinese domestic EMC or SRRC requirements apply; not equivalent to Azerbaijani import filing by themselves.

rows.verdict: [INFORMATIONAL] Do not assume a Chinese EMC package plus CCC and SRRC approvals fully satisfies Azerbaijani entry logic. Products with communication functions may need a separate local radio path and local importer coordination, in addition to battery safety documentation.

source.publisher: AZS and national telecom/radio authority references for Azerbaijan

rows.requirement: Market Entry and In-Country Importer Structure
rows.target_requirement: Azerbaijan market entry for lithium batteries is handled through import-side governance where regulated products require an in-country importer and documentation package prepared for customs and authority checks at Baku. Importers are responsible for coordinating compliance evidence and for maintaining the required local records for post-entry controls.
target_standards: AZS/import framework and customs check requirements for regulated electrical imports
Port of entry procedures for customs and conformity review
rows.china_equivalent: China domestic and export processes rely on exporter declaration and domestic safety certification paths. There is no identical legal requirement for a local importer-of-record process matching Azerbaijan customs and regulator coordination in the same form.
china_standards: GB 31241 and related domestic Chinese lithium-safety baseline
CNCA/CNCA catalogue and domestic customs declaration channels
rows.gap: Chinese exporters must establish Azerbaijani in-country importer readiness even when Chinese-side approvals are complete. Missing local importer readiness is a frequent entry blocker for first-time lanes, especially for Baku-based customs release and post-clearance controls.

mandatory_status.target: Mandatory for regulated import flows requiring in-country importer coordination and local record management.
mandatory_status.cn: Not directly applicable in equivalent form. China's exporter declaration model does not substitute for Azerbaijani in-country importer and local compliance workflow.

rows.verdict: [INFORMATIONAL] This is a high-priority market-entry gap. Chinese exports should be paired with a qualified in-country importer and local documentation preparation for Baku entry before shipment.

rows.target_requirement: Lithium cells and batteries shipped to Azerbaijan from China must pass UN 38.3 testing per the UN Manual of Tests and Criteria, using the standard test set and reporting structure for T1 to T8. Classification, packing, and carriage documentation must match the chosen mode and carrier requirements. Azerbaijan transport acceptance at Baku follows international dangerous-goods logic with UN numbers and Class 9 labelling where applicable.
target_standards: UN Manual of Tests and Criteria, Part III, Section 38.3
UN Model Regulations on the Transport of Dangerous Goods
Dangerous goods carrier documentation requirements for sea and air modes
rows.china_equivalent: China also applies UN 38.3 as the baseline for dangerous-goods exports and uses the same UN numbering and Class 9 framework in international transport. Therefore the technical test framework itself is largely aligned.
rows.gap: The gap is usually administrative: ensuring consignee, Baku entry point, and operator-facing documentation (DGD, declarations, labeling, and packing marks) are complete for Azerbaijani shipment acceptance.

mandatory_status.target: Mandatory for all relevant lithium battery exports because they are dangerous goods under international transport rules and must meet UN 38.3 and documentation obligations.
mandatory_status.cn: Mandatory for lithium battery exports from China in current logistics channels; transport compliance is already a core export requirement.

rows.verdict: [INFORMATIONAL] Transport requirements are largely harmonised between China and Azerbaijan at the UN 38.3 level, but document handover at entry still must be correct. Confirm Baku consignee and dangerous-goods routing before first shipment.

source.publisher: United Nations Economic Commission for Europe (UNECE) — Manual of Tests and Criteria
